# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| red | red |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have the light-to-wire table, but Deaf cannot hear me and we have no established gesture code. I should wait for Deaf to announce a gesture encoding aloud; I can hear it and then use that code to transmit the manual visually.

``` 
wait()
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| red | red |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I can cut wire positions 1, 2, or 3. I currently feel no distinguishing tactile information. Please tell me the manual rule and relay any needed colour or marking question to Deaf.

Blind has asked for the rule, but I cannot speak to Blind. Deaf can speak to Blind, yet Deaf first needs a mutually understood gesture code from me. No code has been announced, so sending arbitrary symbols would not convey the color mapping. I will signal Deaf for attention and wait for Deaf to establish a code aloud.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋"])
wait()
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| red | red |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports: display zero; light red; wires: position one blue, position two red, position three green. Please provide the manual's exact cut instruction.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👋]

Deaf has supplied the necessary observation: the light is red, so the manual requires cutting the red wire, which Deaf identifies as position 2. However, I still have no established visual code by which to tell Deaf “position 2”; an arbitrary gesture could be misunderstood. I will wait for Deaf to announce a gesture/number convention that I can use.

``` 
wait()
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| red | red |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Using the visible state I sent, apply the manual. Then signal your required cut position to Deaf by making the same gesture repeated exactly once for wire 1, twice for wire 2, or three times for wire 3. Use any one gesture symbol consistently; Deaf will describe/count it to me.

The red light requires cutting the red wire. Deaf reported that the red wire is in position 2. Blind has established that repeated instances of one gesture encode the wire position, so I will send Deaf two identical gestures.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👍"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| red | red |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Bomb view again: display 0, red light; wires 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green. Apply the manual, then send exactly one gesture to Deaf: 👍 means cut wire 1; 👎 means cut wire 2; 👌 means cut wire 3; ☝ means do not cut/wait.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [✌]

The light is red, and the manual says to cut the red wire. The visible wiring identifies the red wire as position 2. Under Blind’s newly specified gesture code, 👎 means cut wire 2, so I will send that single gesture to Deaf.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| red | red |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I received that you sent two thumbs. To confirm your manual result: send exactly one 👍 for cut wire 1, exactly two 👍 for cut wire 2, exactly three 👍 for cut wire 3, or exactly one ☝ for wait/no cut. Send only that confirmation to Deaf now.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👉]

The manual still maps the red light to the red wire, and the red wire is position 2. Blind explicitly requests confirmation using the repeated-thumb protocol, so I will send exactly two 👍 gestures to Deaf.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👍"])
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| red | red |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Do not answer yes/no questions. Apply the manual and send Deaf only: one 👍 if cut wire 1, two 👍 if cut wire 2, three 👍 if cut wire 3, or one ☝ if wait. No other symbols. Deaf will relay the exact symbols/count.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🖐]

The red light requires cutting the red wire, which is wire 2. The required encoding is two thumbs-up gestures.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👍"])
```

TURN 8
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| red | red |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Direct confirmation only: does the manual instruct us to cut wire 2? Send Deaf exactly one 👍 for YES, or exactly one 👎 for NO. Send no other gesture.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [✌ 👍 👍]

The manual maps the red light to cutting the red wire, and Deaf identified wire 2 as red. Therefore the answer is yes.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 9
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| red | red |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Final verification: if the manual says cut wire 2, send Deaf exactly two 👍 symbols. If the manual says anything else or says wait, send Deaf exactly one ✋ symbol. Send only the applicable signal.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🖐]

The red light maps to cutting the red wire, which is wire 2. The requested final-verification signal is therefore exactly two thumbs-up symbols.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👍"])
```

TURN 10
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| red | red |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Use only a count code now. Send Deaf repetitions of ONE SAME gesture symbol: 1 repetition means cut wire 1 (blue); 2 repetitions means cut wire 2 (red); 3 repetitions means cut wire 3 (green); 4 repetitions means do not cut/wait. Send exactly one group, with no other gestures.

The red light maps to cutting the red wire, which is wire 2. Under the requested count code, I will send two repetitions of the same gesture.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👍"])
```

TURN 11
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| red | red |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🖐]

The prior cut was accepted, and the bomb has changed. I have no new manual instruction or visible state, so I should wait for Blind or Deaf to provide the next-stage information.

``` 
wait()
```

TURN 12
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| red | red |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Updated bomb state from Deaf: display 0; light yellow; wire 1 blue remains; wire 2 is cut; wire 3 green remains. Apply the manual for the next step. Reply to Deaf with repetitions of one same gesture: 1 means cut wire 1, 2 means cut wire 2, 3 means cut wire 3, 4 means wait/no cut. Send exactly one group.

The yellow light requires cutting the blue wire. The remaining blue wire is position 1, so I will signal one repetition.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```
